title: Streamlined Edge RAG Walkthrough: compact WASM worker adapter & checkpointed streaming quickstart
author: Arielle Moreno
release_notes: Introduce a compact Edge RAG quickstart: WASM worker adapter, checkpointed streaming resume, offline index example, and small telemetry probes. Good first-run for edge deployments and device-constrained inference flows.
description:
Motivation: make it straightforward to run a compact Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) flow in edge environments (Cloudflare Workers/deno-wasm/edge functions) where full Node runtimes are heavyweight. This quickstart shows a tiny WASM 'worker adapter' that runs a lightweight indexer, performs client-side prefix caching, and coordinates streaming responses with checkpointed resume so intermittent connections can resume token streams without losing continuity.

Summary of changes: single continuous documentation quickstart, a minimal adapter (TypeScript for edge + small WASM helper), CI examples for smoke tests, a telemetry probe to validate token continuity, and example curl/devcontainer snippets for local debugging.

Checklist (done):
- [x] Author guide and walkthrough with commands and expected outputs
- [x] Compact WASM helper (TS bindings + adapter shim)
- [x] Checkpointed streaming example and sample session recording
- [x] Offline index example (local sqlite-backed index and incremental updates)
- [x] CI smoke test to validate quickstart builds and basic latency assertions

How to use (excerpt):
1) Clone and open quickstart: cd quickstarts/edge-wasm-quickstart
2) Start local dev proxy (devcontainer recommended): ./scripts/dev-proxy.sh --local
3) Build wasm helper and edge adapter: ./scripts/build-wasm && ./scripts/build-adapter
4) Publish a small index: node scripts/seed-index.js ./data/sample-corpus.json
5) Run the edge shim locally and open the replay page: yarn start:replay
6) Trigger a streaming RAG request with checkpoint resume header: 
   curl -N -H 'X-RAG-RESUME: session-123' -d '{"q":"How do I scale prefix caches on edge?"}' http://localhost:8080/api/ask
Expected: streaming chunks with resume points (X-STREAM-CHECKPOINT) and a final stable answer.

Small snippets included (in docs):
- Edge adapter (adapter.ts) shows how to call Redwood API with prefer_low_latency routing and how to include checkpoint tokens in the streaming loop.
- wasm/helper.ts demonstrates a tiny tokenizer + KV helper compiled to wasm for quick prefix matching (source and TS bindings included).

Notes on compatibility and scope: 
- This quickstart intentionally avoids heavy server-side components; the indexer is sqlite-backed with an incremental writer to keep memory small on edge devices. For production workloads we recommend using Redwood Dedicated with a managed indexer and caching policies — see 'When to move off the quickstart' in the README.

Why this is different: existing quickstarts cover RAG at various scales (serverless, local dev, and full orchestrator). This change targets constrained edge runtimes and demonstrates practical tradeoffs (wasm tokenizers, checkpointed streaming resume, and small persistent indexes). It also provides a clean pattern for teams that need to ship RAG features into CDN-edge or offline-capable clients.
